title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: people data with source-system access controls
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned people-data access controls from today's documented everyone-access requirement. The roadmap details and existing connector controls are supported; the new capability's default, licensing and migration process remain unpublished.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to support importing people data together with source-system ACLs.
claims.quote: This release enables organizations to bring people data from external systems into Microsoft 365 along with associated access control lists (ACLs)

claims.claim: The planned capability makes Copilot respect permissions defined in source systems.
claims.quote: ensuring Copilot respects existing permissions defined in source systems.

claims.claim: Imported people data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups in the planned capability.
claims.quote: The imported data can be scoped to specific individuals and groups

claims.claim: Copilot will be able to reason over imported people data while honouring access restrictions.
claims.quote: allowing Copilot to reason over people data while honoring access restrictions.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[0].note; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Today's people-connector documentation says imported people data is visible to all tenant users by default.
claims.quote: By default, people data provided via a Copilot connector is visible to all users in the tenant.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Today's people-connector build guide requires ingested items to grant everyone access in their ACL.
claims.quote: You must set the access control list (ACL) on items ingested by the connector to grant access to everyone.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the roadmap's differentiated people-data ACL capability.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access control ACL individuals groups default existing connections migration 561326. Opened graph/peopleconnectors and extensibility/build-connectors-with-people-data; both still describe everyone-visible data.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Custom people connectors are built using Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.
claims.quote: You build Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data in the same way that you build other Copilot connectors, by using the Microsoft Graph external connections APIs.

claims.claim: A people-data connection must set contentCategory to people.
claims.quote: Copilot connectors that contain people data must have the value `people` in the `contentCategory` property of the `externalConnections` API.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Imported people-connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.
claims.quote: This connector data is stored in the user's Microsoft 365 profile.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Uploaded people-data attributes are stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: When you upload people data, each user's data attributes are scoped to their Microsoft 365 user profile and stored in the user's Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the new ACL capability's default state.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access control ACL individuals groups default existing connections migration 561326. Read the roadmap, graph/peopleconnectors and the people-data build guide; none specifies the new ACL control's default.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented migration of existing everyone-ACL people connections, including whether they change automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access control ACL individuals groups default existing connections migration 561326; people connectors access control default migration. Opened peopleconnectors, the people-data build guide and manage-access-permissions; no people-ACL migration is described.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The general connector permissions page says updating access permissions after connection creation is not supported.
claims.quote: Updating access permissions after you create the connection isn't currently supported.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The general permissions guidance describes deleting the connection and recreating it with Custom setup to change its visibility model.
claims.quote:
In the connector pane, choose Delete to delete the existing connection.
Recreate the connection using the Custom setup flow and explicitly configure access permissions.

claims.claim: Ingested people data can be surfaced by Copilot and people search.
claims.quote: Adding people data to Microsoft Graph makes it available to Microsoft 365 Copilot and people experiences such as the profile card and people search.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No admin UI, PowerShell cmdlet or Graph API is yet documented for the planned differentiated people-data ACL control.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access control ACL individuals groups default existing connections migration 561326; people connectors ACL PowerShell. Opened peopleconnectors, the build guide and Graph externalConnection v1.0/beta references; people items still require everyone ACLs.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented how differentiated people-data ACLs will affect profile cards, Org Explorer and search.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors ACL PowerShell Graph differentiated access profile cards Org Explorer information barriers migration. Opened peopleconnectors and the people-data build guide; existing surfaces are described, but not future ACL enforcement across them.

claims.claim: People connectors comply with Microsoft Purview Information Barriers.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors for people data comply with information barriers (IB) to ensure compliance across various platforms.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explained how Information Barriers interact with the planned per-person ACLs.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors ACL PowerShell Graph differentiated access profile cards Org Explorer information barriers migration. Opened peopleconnectors and the build guide; neither explains interactions between IB and the planned differentiated ACLs.

claims.claim: People-data ingestion ignores accounts whose identifiers do not match a user.
claims.quote: Nonmatched user accounts (`userPrincipalName` or `externalDirectoryObjectId`) are ignored.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.
claims.quote: Microsoft Graph ignores accounts without an Exchange Online mailbox.

claims.claim: The sources describe ingestion and grounding rather than a new source-system write-action capability.
claims.quote: Searched: people connectors differentiated access control ACL individuals groups default existing connections migration 561326. Read the roadmap, peopleconnectors and the people-data build guide; these describe importing data and using it for reasoning, not new source-system write actions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Connections carrying people data do not support staged connections.
claims.quote: Connections with people data don't support staged connections.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft separately recommends piloting people connectors with a limited audience.
claims.quote: Before rollout, confirm governance, privacy, and admin requirements for your connector and pilot with a limited audience.

claims.claim: Connector-ingested people properties are read-only to users.
claims.quote: All properties ingested via the people connectors are read-only.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends disabling user edits of overlapping properties to avoid edits not appearing on profile cards.
claims.quote: We recommend that you disable user editing of any properties that are also ingested via people connectors to avoid scenarios where user edits aren't displayed on the profile card due to the precedence model.

claims.claim: The general prerequisites page lists Microsoft 365 plus the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on, or Microsoft 365 E7, for synced-connector Copilot grounding and agents.

Microsoft 365 + Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on | ✅ | ✅ | ✅
Microsoft 365 E7 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅

claims.claim: In the general connector eligibility table, Microsoft 365 alone supports synced-connector Microsoft Search but not Copilot grounding and agents.
claims.quote:

Microsoft 365 (any plan) | ✅ | ❌ | ❌

claims.quote: Indexing of synced connector data incurs no extra cost for tenants with Microsoft 365 licenses.

claims.claim: The general connector prerequisites page does not specifically mention people connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors differentiated ACL licensing pricing meter spending cap. Read connectors/prerequisites in full; it covers synced and federated connector prerequisites and licensing, without specifically naming people connectors.

claims.claim: No meter specific to the planned ACL capability is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors differentiated ACL licensing pricing meter spending cap. Opened peopleconnectors, the build guide and connectors/prerequisites; no meter specific to the future ACL capability is documented.

claims.claim: No credit rate specific to the planned ACL capability is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors differentiated ACL licensing pricing meter spending cap. Opened peopleconnectors, the build guide and connectors/prerequisites; none specifies a credit rate for the planned ACL capability.

claims.claim: No spending cap specific to the planned ACL capability is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: people data connectors differentiated ACL licensing pricing meter spending cap. Opened peopleconnectors, the build guide, connectors/prerequisites and Graph connection management; none documents an ACL-specific spending cap.

claims.claim: People data persists while the user is active and holds a valid Microsoft 365 licence, subject to the deletion behaviour described elsewhere on the page.
claims.quote: People data is stored as long as the end user is active and has a valid Microsoft 365 license, provided no deletion request was made by the admin.

`personCurrentPosition` | `string` | workPosition

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented Permissions path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Permissions.
claims.quote:
go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections.
Select the connector you want to review to open the details pane.
Under Permissions, you can view the permissions set for the connector.

claims.claim: No API is documented for the connector-level Permissions view's source-ACL-versus-everyone model.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph connectors view connection Permissions source ACL everyone API PowerShell. Opened manage-access-permissions and externalConnection v1.0/beta references; found item ACL APIs but no API for this connector-level Permissions view/model.

claims.claim: Partner-connector visibility is controlled at Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections > select the connection > Copilot Visibility in Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote:
Go to Copilot > Connectors > Your Connections.
Select the connection that you want to modify.
Under Copilot Visibility, select the toggle to turn the connector on or off, and choose Save.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of the documented Copilot Visibility toggle is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph connector Copilot Visibility toggle API enabledContentExperiences update externalConnection; Copilot Visibility Graph beta. Opened manage-connector, externalConnection v1.0/beta and Update externalConnection; none documents this toggle's API equivalent.

claims.claim: The management page describes Copilot Visibility for partner connectors without confirming applicability to people connectors.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph connector Copilot Visibility toggle API enabledContentExperiences update externalConnection. Read manage-connector and peopleconnectors; the toggle is described for partner connectors, with no confirmation for people connectors.

claims.claim: Admin UI creation of custom people-data connectors is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: custom people data connector create Microsoft 365 admin center user interface. Opened peopleconnectors, the build guide and manage-connector; Microsoft-built people connectors have UI setup, while custom people-data connectors use Graph APIs.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections creates the external connection used for people data, with its people contentCategory requirement checked separately.
claims.quote:
Create a new externalConnection object.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections
In the request body, supply a JSON representation of the externalConnection object.

claims.claim: A people connector can be deleted in Microsoft 365 admin center from Connectors > Your Connections > select the connector > Delete.
claims.quote:
Go to the Microsoft 365 admin center and navigate to the connectors section.
On the Your Connections tab, select the connector you want to delete.
Select the Delete option.

claims.claim: DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/{connectionId} deletes an external connection.
Deleting a people connector removes it from all instances, but delays can be expected.
claims.quote: If a connector is deleted, it's removed from all instances, but delays can be expected.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents the Permissions view for each Microsoft 365 Copilot connector.
claims.quote: You can review and validate access permissions for each Microsoft 365 Copilot connector from the connection details pane in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: The Permissions view distinguishes respecting source-system ACLs from granting visibility to everyone.
claims.quote:
Only people with access to this data source: The connector respects source system access control lists (ACLs).
Visible to everyone: The connector grants access to all users in the organization.

claims.claim: Turning off the documented partner-connector visibility control excludes that connector from Copilot Search and Copilot Chat results and responses.
claims.quote: When the visibility is off, the connector is excluded from all Copilot Search and Copilot Chat results and responses.
